title: Unbounded étale to pro-étale comparison from finite étale cohomological dimension
statement: Let A be a finite commutative ring and g:X→Y a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes. Use the ordinary module-sheaf unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] and comparison inverse images [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Assume there is d∈ℕ such that R^q g_et,* M=0 for every A-module sheaf M and every q>d. For every K∈D(X_et,A), the actual mate ν_Y^* Rg_et,* K→Rg_proet,* ν_X^* K of the canonical derived pullback comparison square is invertible. There is no boundedness assumption on K and no cohomological-dimension assumption for arbitrary pro-étale sheaves.

source.place: lemma-morphism-comparison (bounded-below canonical mate); literature/stacks-project/derived.tex, Tag 07K7 (finite cohomological dimension); left-completeness truncation argument as in lem-sfb-derived-left-complete-truncation-bound.

proof.text: Normalize the native total-left-derived comparison functors to their exact termwise mapDerivedCategory models by their canonical isomorphisms. The resulting natural transformation is a conjugate of the specified mate; invertibility of either one is equivalent to invertibility of the other. The uniform heart bound puts Rg_et,* of an upper-bounded object L in degrees at most b+d, and exact comparison preserves the bound.

On every lower truncation of L, bounded-below comparison identifies Rg_proet,* ν_X^* with ν_Y^* Rg_et,*. Exact comparison commutes with truncation, so every image of a truncation of ν_X^*L has upper bound b+d. Pro-étale modules have exact countable products, and Rg_proet,* preserves products as a right adjoint. The left-completeness Milnor triangle therefore puts its value on ν_X^*L in degrees at most b+d+1. No claim of finite cohomological dimension for all pro-étale sheaves is made.

For any degree m choose N=m-d-2. The first term τ_<N K of the truncation triangle has upper bound N-1. The two functors just bounded send it to degrees at most N-1+d and N+d respectively, so H^m and H^(m+1) vanish. The homology long exact sequences make the maps from their values on K to the values on τ_>=N K isomorphisms in degree m.

Naturality gives a square with these two invertible degree-m truncation maps and the bounded-below comparison on τ_>=N K. Thus the specified comparison on K is invertible on H^m, for every m. Homology detects isomorphisms; conjugating back gives invertibility of the original native mate. Empty schemes, zero rings and complexes unbounded in both directions are included.
